mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 750e engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 7 Series 750e engine replacement typically costs £2,000-£3,800 for a used B58B30S unit, £3,800-£6,000 for a reconditioned engine, and £5,000-£8,000 for a fully rebuilt engine with warranty. Supply & fit adds £650-£910 in specialist labour (10-14 hours). Note that the 750e's hybrid system adds complexity, and the high-voltage battery is a separate cost centre.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of PCV valve failure in a BMW 7 Series 750e?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include rough idle, engine misfires, oil in the intake or charge pipe, blue or white smoke from the exhaust on cold start, and a whistling or squealing noise from the engine. The PCV valve is a known weakness on the B58 engine, particularly on cars with upgraded turbos.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 750e?

acceptedAnswer.text: With values ranging from £50,000 to £109,000, a full rebuilt engine at £5,000-£8,000 represents just 5-15% of the vehicle's value - making replacement financially viable for most examples. However, the hybrid battery may also need attention, with replacement costs of £7,000-£10,000+.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 750e engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 7 Series 750e engine replacement takes 3-5 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The B58 straight-six has good engine bay access, but the hybrid system's high-voltage components require additional safety precautions and specialist knowledge. Most specialists offer collection/delivery options nationwide with same-day dispatch available for in-stock engines.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 750e and 740i engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 740i uses the B58 straight-six producing 375hp with no hybrid assistance. The 750e uses the same B58 engine (308hp) paired with a 194hp electric motor for a combined 489hp and 700Nm of torque. The 750e offers 36 miles of electric-only range, lower CO2 emissions (25g/km), and significantly better fuel economy in city driving.

The B58 engine is considered one of BMW's most reliable modern engines, with a strong reputation for durability. The PCV valve is the main weakness. The hybrid system adds complexity, but BMW's PHEV technology is mature. However, the 22.1kWh battery will degrade over time, and replacement costs can be significant (£7,000-£10,000+).

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 750e Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 7 Series 750e is powered by the B58B30S 3.0-litre turbo straight-six - one of BMW's most reliable modern engines - paired with a 194hp electric motor and a 22.1kWh battery. While the B58 is significantly more reliable than older BMW engines, the hybrid system adds complexity and potential failure points. Rebuilt 750e engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: PCV Valve Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 750e B58 Misfires
problems.rootCause: The B58 engine's PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve can fail, causing a vacuum leak that leads to rough idle, misfires, and oil in the intake tract. This issue is particularly common on cars with upgraded turbos and can cause blue/white smoke from the exhaust on cold start.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace PCV valve, clean intake, reset adaptations
Supply & fit, upgraded PCV system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if PCV failure has caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 7 Series 750e currently values between £50,000 and £109,000 depending on mileage and specification, with M Sport examples commanding a premium. A full rebuilt engine at £5,000-£8,000 represents 5-15% of the vehicle's value - well within the "safe" threshold for most examples.
problems.recommendation: If your 750e is misfiring or idling roughly, have the PCV valve checked first. The B58 is generally a reliable engine, and a PCV valve replacement is a straightforward fix that addresses the most common failure point.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B58B30S BMW 7 Series 750e engine prices

problems.h4: High-Voltage Battery Degradation - Why the BMW 7 Series 750e Loses Electric Range
problems.rootCause: Like all lithium-ion batteries, the 750e's 22.1kWh battery pack will degrade over time, reducing electric range and performance. The battery has a usable energy content of 14.4 kWh. Extreme temperatures and frequent rapid charging can accelerate degradation.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if only one or two modules are failing
Necessary if multiple modules have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A full battery replacement at £7,000-£10,000 represents 10-20% of the vehicle's value - significant but still viable for high-value examples. For lower-value 750es approaching £50,000, carefully evaluate whether the investment is worthwhile.
problems.recommendation: Monitor your 750e's electric range regularly. If you notice a significant drop (20%+), have the battery health checked by a BMW specialist. Individual module replacement is often more cost-effective than a full battery replacement if caught early.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for BMW 7 Series 750e hybrid battery replacement

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the BMW 7 Series 750e B58 Rattles
problems.rootCause: The B58 engine's timing chain tensioner can wear over time, causing the chain to become loose. This results in a rattling noise from the engine, particularly on cold starts. If left unaddressed, chain wear can lead to timing drift and potential engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner, inspect chain and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before chain stretch
Necessary if chain has stretched significantly

repairOptions.longevity: Only if chain failure has caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A timing chain tensioner replacement at £500-£900 is negligible relative to the vehicle's value. A full timing chain replacement at £1,500-£2,500 represents 2-5% of the vehicle's value. A full engine replacement at £5,000-£8,000 is still only 5-15% of the vehicle's value - well within the "safe" threshold.
problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling from the engine on cold starts, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately - a £50-£100 inspection could save you thousands. A tensioner replacement is much cheaper than a full timing chain job or engine replacement.
